title: Uniformizer presentation of a totally ramified complete DVR extension
statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $E/F$ be a finite separable field extension of degree $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and let $S\subset E$ be the integral closure of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume $S$ is a discrete valuation ring, that $R\to S$ is local, that the induced map $R/\mathfrak m_R\to S/\mathfrak m_S$ is an isomorphism, and that $\mathfrak m_RS=\mathfrak m_S^n$. For every uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$ and every uniformizer $t$ of $S$, there is a polynomial $P(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}a_iT^i\in R[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $a_i\in\pi R$ for all $i<n$ and $a_0\in\pi R\setminus\pi^2R$, such that evaluation $T\mapsto t$ induces isomorphisms $R[T]/(P)\cong S$ and $F[T]/(P)\cong E$. Local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal; finite degree means vector-space dimension.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: Since R is a DVR, it is a PID and hence Noetherian and normal. Apply IsIntegralClosure.finite to obtain that S is finite over R. Apply the existing integral-closure rank theorem IsIntegralClosure.rank to get finrank_R S = finrank_F E = n. The finite algebraic normalization also has E as its localization at the nonzero elements of R, by IsIntegralClosure.isLocalization; this is the localization used in the rank theorem.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: Surjectivity on residue fields gives, for each s in S, an r in R and y in S with s = r + t y. Induct on k to expand s as sum_{i<k} r_i t^i + t^k y. At k=n the remainder lies in m_R S, because m_R S = m_S^n = (t^n). Thus the images of 1,t,...,t^(n-1) span S/m_R S. This is a finite induction, with no use of completeness or infinite series.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: Nakayama (IsLocalRing.map_mkQ_eq_top) applied to the finite R-module S shows that the n powers span S itself. Their cardinality equals finrank_R S by step 1, so Mathlib basisOfTopLeSpanOfCardEqFinrank makes precisely these vectors a basis. This uses the Orzech property of the Noetherian ring R, as encoded in that theorem. Package the basis as a PowerBasis pb with gen=t and dim=n; no valuation-order independence argument is needed.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: The uniformizer and ramification equalities give (pi)S=(t^n). Choose v,w in S with t^n=pi*v and pi=t^n*w. Since t is nonzero, cancellation of t^n gives w*v=1, so v is a unit.

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: Set P=pb.minpolyGen, the monic degree-n polynomial X^n minus the coordinate expansion of t^n in the basis. If c_i are the R-coordinates of v, linearity of the coordinate map and t^n=pi*v give P.coeff i = -pi*c_i for every i<n. All required lower coefficients therefore lie in (pi). If the constant coefficient lay in (pi^2), cancellation of nonzero pi would put c_0 in m_R. In the coordinate expansion v=sum c_i*t^i, its constant term would then belong to m_S by locality, while every remaining term belongs to m_S because t does and i>0. This would make the unit v a nonunit. Hence P.coeff 0 is not in (pi^2).

source.place: Tag 09ER, lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified, proof: first paragraph, from the choice of uniformizers through the displayed minimal polynomial and e=[K_1:K]

proof.text: The standard PowerBasis and AdjoinRoot equivalence for the basis polynomial gives R[X]/(P) isomorphic to S by evaluation at t. Localize the same basis along R to F and S to E, using Basis.localizationLocalization and the localization from step 1. Its vectors are the images t^i, and its coordinate maps on S are the original coordinate maps followed by R to F. Consequently its basis polynomial equals P.map (algebraMap R F), term by term. Apply the same AdjoinRoot.equiv' construction to this localized power basis. Both equivalences satisfy the requested evaluation identities by AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom_mk.

Step 1: DVR is a PID, so pid-noetherian-normal gives R and S Noetherian and R normal; 032L-finite gives S finite over R; the integral-closure node gives Frac(S)=E. Step 2: pi=u t^n with u a unit, by cancellation. Step 3: S=R+tS iterated n times, so the t^i span S/m_R S. Step 4: Nakayama local generators, with S finite and R local, gives S=R[t]. Step 5: the unit-times-power leaf gives distinct exponents nk_i+i mod n, so a unique least term and linear independence. Step 6: each nonzero a_i is a unit times pi^k, so the least-exponent rule applies; this gives a_i in pi R, then b_0 a unit via the local map, so a_0 is not in pi^2 R. Step 7: division by monic P gives kernel (P). Step 8: S[1/pi]=Frac(S)=E via the factorization of S, with independence over F by clearing denominators. Edge cases checked: n=1 (P=T-t), Z_p(sqrt p), arbitrary pairs (pi,t), wild ramification and equal characteristic. lean.statement: theorem exists_uniformizer_polynomial_presentation (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] (F : Type v) [Field F] [Algebra R F] [IsFractionRing R F] (E : Type w) [Field E] [Algebra F E] [Algebra R E] [IsScalarTower R F E] [FiniteDimensional F E] [Algebra.IsSeparable F E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hdegree : Module.finrank F E = n) (S : Subalgebra R E) (hS : S = integralClosure R E) [IsDiscreteValuationRing S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (hresidue : Function.Bijective (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap R S))) (hramification : (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) = maximalIdeal S ^ n) (pi : R) (hpi : maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {pi}) (t : S) (ht : maximalIdeal S = Ideal.span {t}) : ∃ P : R[X], P.Monic ∧ P.natDegree = n ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, i < n → P.coeff i ∈ Ideal.span {pi}) ∧ P.coeff 0 ∉ Ideal.span {pi ^ 2} ∧ (∃ e : (R[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {P}) ≃ₐ[R] S, ∀ Q : R[X], e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {P}) Q) = aeval t Q) ∧ (∃ e : (F[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {P.map (algebraMap R F)}) ≃ₐ[F] E, ∀ Q : F[X], e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {P.map (algebraMap R F)}) Q) = aeval (t : E) Q)
